objects.description: Enumeration of JSON parsing strategies: STANDARD (no comments) and COMMENTS (allow comments).

Primary value type representing any JSON value. Value-semantics wrapper around a shared_ptr to an internal JsonValue hierarchy. Provides construction from native types, containers, serialization (dump), parsing (parse/parse_multi), accessors, comparisons, and shape validation.
Enumeration of the kind of JSON value contained by json11::Json instances.
Alias for JSON array container type used by Json, representing a dynamic array of Json values.
Alias for JSON object container type used by Json, mapping strings to Json values.
Helper alias representing an expected "shape" of a JSON object: a list of field name and expected Json::Type pairs, used by has_shape.

Abstract base class for the internal polymorphic representation of Json values. Not exposed publicly; managed via shared_ptr by Json. Provides virtual interface for type, comparison, serialization, and typed accessors. Concrete subclasses (e.g., JsonInt, JsonDouble) are referenced but not defined in this header.

functions.name: json11::Json::Json
functions.description: Default constructor. Constructs a null (NUL) JSON value. Useful as a sentinel or to represent JSON null.

functions.name: json11::Json::Json
functions.description: Constructs a null (NUL) JSON value from a nullptr literal, representing JSON null.

functions.name: json11::Json::Json
functions.description: Constructs a NUMBER JSON value from a double. json11 stores numbers internally as double.

functions.name: json11::Json::Json
functions.description: Constructs a NUMBER JSON value from an int. Internally stored as double but provides integer helpers.

functions.name: json11::Json::Json
functions.description: Constructs a BOOL JSON value.

functions.name: json11::Json::Json
functions.description: Constructs a STRING JSON value from a const std::string&.

functions.name: json11::Json::Json
functions.description: Constructs a STRING JSON value by moving from an rvalue std::string.

functions.name: json11::Json::Json
functions.description: Constructs a STRING JSON value from a C-string.
requirements: value must point to a valid, null-terminated string. Behavior is unspecified if value is an invalid pointer.

functions.name: json11::Json::Json
functions.description: Constructs an ARRAY JSON value from a container of Json elements.

functions.name: json11::Json::Json
functions.description: Constructs an ARRAY JSON value by moving from an rvalue array of Json elements.

functions.description: Constructs an OBJECT JSON value from a map of string keys to Json values.

functions.name: json11::Json::type
functions.description: Returns the runtime type tag of this JSON value (NUL, NUMBER, BOOL, STRING, ARRAY, or OBJECT).

functions.name: json11::Json::is_null
functions.description: Convenience check for type() == NUL.

functions.name: json11::Json::is_number
functions.description: Convenience check for type() == NUMBER.

functions.name: json11::Json::is_bool
functions.description: Convenience check for type() == BOOL.

functions.name: json11::Json::is_string
functions.description: Convenience check for type() == STRING.

functions.name: json11::Json::is_array
functions.description: Convenience check for type() == ARRAY.

functions.name: json11::Json::is_object
functions.description: Convenience check for type() == OBJECT.

functions.name: json11::Json::number_value
functions.description: If this is a NUMBER, returns the enclosed numeric value; otherwise returns 0. json11 does not distinguish between integer and non-integer numbers internally.

functions.name: json11::Json::int_value
functions.description: If this is a NUMBER, returns the numeric value converted to int; otherwise returns 0. Provided as an integer helper over the internal double.

functions.name: json11::Json::bool_value
functions.description: If this is a BOOL, returns the enclosed boolean; otherwise returns false.

functions.name: json11::Json::string_value
functions.description: If this is a STRING, returns a reference to the enclosed std::string; otherwise returns a reference to an empty string.
requirements: The returned reference remains valid as long as the Json value from which it was obtained remains valid. Exact lifetime and aliasing semantics beyond that are not specified in this header.

functions.name: json11::Json::array_items
functions.description: If this is an ARRAY, returns a reference to the enclosed std::vector<Json>; otherwise returns a reference to an empty vector.
requirements: The returned reference remains valid as long as the Json value from which it was obtained remains valid. Exact mutation semantics are not specified in this header.

functions.name: json11::Json::object_items
functions.description: If this is an OBJECT, returns a reference to the enclosed std::map<std::string, Json>; otherwise returns a reference to an empty map.
requirements: The returned reference remains valid as long as the Json value from which it was obtained remains valid. Exact mutation semantics are not specified in this header.

functions.name: json11::Json::operator[]
functions.description: Array indexing. If this is an ARRAY, returns a reference to element at index i; otherwise returns a reference to a null Json (Json()).
requirements: If this is an ARRAY and i is out of bounds, the behavior per comment is to return Json(); callers should not assume exceptions are thrown for out-of-range access.
No mutation is performed; result is const reference.

functions.name: json11::Json::operator[]
functions.signature: const json11::Json& json11::Json::operator[](const std::string& key) const
functions.description: Object lookup. If this is an OBJECT, returns a reference to the value at key; otherwise returns a reference to a null Json (Json()).
requirements: If key is not present in an OBJECT, the behavior per comment is to return Json(); callers should not assume insertion or exceptions.
No mutation is performed; result is const reference.

functions.name: json11::Json::dump
functions.description: Serializes this Json value into a string buffer. Use to produce a JSON-encoded representation.
requirements: out must be a valid std::string reference.
Whether serialization appends to or overwrites out is not specified in this header; callers should not rely on either behavior without consulting the implementation.

functions.name: json11::Json::dump
functions.description: Serializes this Json value and returns the resulting JSON-encoded string. Convenience wrapper around dump(std::string&).

functions.name: json11::Json::parse
functions.signature: static json11::Json json11::Json::parse(const std::string& in, std::string& err, json11::JsonParse strategy = json11::JsonParse::STANDARD)
functions.description: Parses the input string into a Json value. On failure, returns Json() and assigns an error message to err. The strategy parameter controls parsing mode (STANDARD or COMMENTS).
requirements: err must be a valid std::string reference and will be assigned on failure.
in may contain one JSON value. Behavior for additional trailing data is not specified here.
strategy selects parsing policy; valid values are json11::JsonParse::STANDARD or json11::JsonParse::COMMENTS.

functions.name: json11::Json::parse
functions.signature: static json11::Json json11::Json::parse(const char* in, std::string& err, json11::JsonParse strategy = json11::JsonParse::STANDARD)
functions.description: Parses the C-string input into a Json value. If in is null, sets err to "null input" and returns a null Json (nullptr). On other failures, returns Json() and assigns an error message to err.
requirements: in must be a valid, null-terminated C-string; passing nullptr is allowed and results in an error as described.
err must be a valid std::string reference and will be assigned on failure.
strategy selects parsing policy; valid values are json11::JsonParse::STANDARD or json11::JsonParse::COMMENTS.

functions.name: json11::Json::parse_multi
functions.signature: static std::vector<json11::Json> json11::Json::parse_multi(const std::string& in, std::string::size_type& parser_stop_pos, std::string& err, json11::JsonParse strategy = json11::JsonParse::STANDARD)
functions.description: Parses multiple JSON objects from a single input string, concatenated or separated by whitespace. Returns a vector of parsed Json values. On failure, returns what was parsed (if any) and assigns an error message to err. parser_stop_pos receives the position where parsing stopped.
requirements: in may contain multiple concatenated or whitespace-separated JSON objects.
parser_stop_pos must be a valid reference and will be set to the index where the parser stopped.
err must be a valid std::string reference and will be assigned on failure.
strategy selects parsing policy; valid values are json11::JsonParse::STANDARD or json11::JsonParse::COMMENTS.

functions.name: json11::Json::parse_multi
functions.signature: static std::vector<json11::Json> json11::Json::parse_multi(const std::string& in, std::string& err, json11::JsonParse strategy = json11::JsonParse::STANDARD)
functions.description: Parses multiple JSON objects from a single input string, concatenated or separated by whitespace. Convenience wrapper that discards the final stop position.
requirements: in may contain multiple concatenated or whitespace-separated JSON objects.
err must be a valid std::string reference and will be assigned on failure.
strategy selects parsing policy; valid values are json11::JsonParse::STANDARD or json11::JsonParse::COMMENTS.

functions.name: json11::Json::operator==
functions.description: Compares two Json values for equality based on their types and contents.

functions.name: json11::Json::operator<
functions.description: Provides a strict weak ordering for Json values to allow use in ordered containers and comparisons.

functions.name: json11::Json::operator!=
functions.description: Inequality comparison; logical negation of operator==.

functions.name: json11::Json::operator<=
functions.description: Less-than-or-equal comparison; defined in terms of operator<.

functions.name: json11::Json::operator>
functions.description: Greater-than comparison; defined in terms of operator<.

functions.name: json11::Json::operator>=
functions.description: Greater-than-or-equal comparison; defined in terms of operator<.

functions.name: json11::Json::has_shape
functions.signature: bool json11::Json::has_shape(const json11::Json::shape& types, std::string& err) const
functions.description: Validates that this Json is an OBJECT and, for each entry in types, contains a field with the given name and Json::Type. Returns true on success; otherwise returns false and sets err to a descriptive message.
requirements: types is an initializer-list or compatible container of name/type pairs to check.
err must be a valid std::string reference and will be assigned on failure.
This function expects the Json to be an OBJECT; otherwise it fails and describes the mismatch.

data_types.description: A generic byte string with no required structure or encoding. May contain any characters including null bytes when held in std::string; used as opaque text for keys or values without format constraints.

Text that should be a JSON document per RFC 7159/8259 (objects, arrays, strings, numbers, booleans, or null). In this context it may also include comments when the COMMENTS strategy is selected. Can be a single JSON value; for parse_multi, can be multiple concatenated or whitespace-separated JSON values.
